title: 1.3.0.Alpha2: Kubernetes Client: Could not initialize class KubernetesDeserializer in dev mode
body:
**Describe the bug**
My previously working code, which is getting the currently running deployments via the Quarkus Kubernetes Client, throws the exception below when run in dev mode (`./gradlew quarkusDev`). This happens with Quarkus 1.3.0.Alpha2 and worked with 1.2 and 1.2.1 (it does not compile with 1.3.0.Alpha1 due to unresolved artifacts). I attached a minimized reproducer project below.

**Expected behavior**
My code should work. 

**Actual behavior**
The code crashes when it tries to retrieve the currently running deployments. This happens in a method called by observing the `StartupEvent` as well as in the health check. I was able to find two workarounds, both shown in the reproducer in the class `DoKubernetesRequestOnStartService` and marked with comments starting with `FIX 1` and `FIX 2`. See the reproduction steps below.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Download the reproducer project 
[quarkus-kubernetes-client-deserializer-missing.zip](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/files/4224324/quarkus-kubernetes-client-deserializer-missing.zip)
 and unpack it.
2. In the project directory, execute `./gradlew quarkusDev`
3. When the server is started, the log will display the exception shown above.
4. The same happens if you, call the health endpoint by querying GET `http://localhost:8080/health`.

5. Workaround 1: When you comment in line DoKubernetesRequestOnStartService:24 (marked with comment `FIX 1: ...`), the number of deployments will be retrieved on start. Also the health check will work.
6. Woraround 2: When you instead comment in the lines DoKubernetesRequestOnStartService:41-45 (marked with comment `FIX 2: ...`) and start the server, the initial retrieval of the deployments is delayed by 5 seconds. If you call the health endpoint during this time frame, it will all work fine. If you do not call the health endpoint in these 5 seconds, the same exception will be thrown as before and the health check will also not work afterwards.

**Configuration**
None

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Windows 10
 - Same for Oracle JDK 1.8.0_231 and Oracle JDK 11.0.4
 - Default of Quarkus 1.3.0.Alpha2
 - Quarkus version or git rev: Quarkus 1.3.0.Alpha2. Works with 1.2.0 and 1.2.1
 - Kubernetes on Docker for Windows (simply activated in the UI)
